title: What happens to 50 family lines?
hook: Trace 50 women's mothers back, generation after generation. Do their lines ever meet?

doesNotKnow: that tracing mothers back, all lines must merge into one woman, after about 2N generations, and she had many contemporaries

misconception: A single common maternal ancestor means there was once only one woman.
objective: The learner can explain that maternal lines join whenever two women share a mother and never split again, so all 50 lines must meet in one woman (about 97 generations back on average here), and that she lived among 49 other women whose lines died out.

claims.text: In 1,000 seeded runs with 50 women per generation, all maternal lines met in one ancestor, on average 96 generations back (median 84); the stage's family met 99 generations back.
claims.source: Builder's own code (meetTime/family in Demo.tsx), re-run in node 2026-10-14 via a transpile-only harness. Haploid Wright–Fisher, N = 50, each generation every distinct line draws mother = floor(rand × 50) from mulberry32(seed). 1,000 runs use seeds 7001–8000 as briefed: all met; mean 96.03, median 84, min 18, max 371, 10th–90th percentile 44–169. The stage's family uses seed 7004, chosen because its meeting time (99) is near the mean and fits the 0–120 axis; it is an illustration, not evidence. Seed 7004 lines: 50 today → 32 one generation back → 23 at 2 → 9 at 12 → 3 at 50 → 2 at 89 → 1 at 99. · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Own mulberry32 copy of meetTime(): seeds 7001-8000 all met, mean 96.033 (reveal rounds to 96), median 84, min 18, max 371; seed 7004 meets at 99, with 32, 23, 9, 3, 2 lines at 1, 2, 12, 50, 89 back. The 'thousand' milestone forces the run, so the reveal always quotes the computed mean.

claims.text: Theory for this model with 50 women expects about 97 generations; 2N(1 − 1/N) = 98 is an approximation.
claims.source: Exact expectation for the discrete model: Markov chain on the number of lines, transition = occupancy of N = 50 bins by k draws; E = 96.97 (exactExpectation in Demo.tsx, builder re-run 2026-10-14; matches the spec's node check). 2N(1 − 1/N) = Σ_{k=2..N} N / C(k,2) = 98 is the continuous-time coalescent approximation for haploid Wright–Fisher (brief claim 2, worded as an approximation per cm-life-genetics-evolution's edit). The 1,000-run mean (96.0) sits within sampling error of 97 (standard error about 1.6). · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Own exact expectation by value iteration on the lines Markov chain (occupancy transitions, 20,000 sweeps): 96.971, rounds to 97; 2N(1 - 1/N) = 98 for N = 50. | REVISED v2 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave G): Reveal wording shortened to 'Theory for 50 expects about 97; 2N(1 − 1/N) = 98 is an approximation.' Same numbers (exactExpectation() and APPROX). | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED (v2 wording). Own value iteration on the lines Markov chain (occupancy transitions): E = 96.971 for N = 50, rounds to 97; 2N(1 - 1/N) = 98 (JS prints exactly 98). Reveal prints Math.round(EXACT) and APPROX; it is inside the mean !== null branch, which every reveal reaches (thousand is required). | v3 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): WITHDRAWN: the theory sentence ("Theory for 50 expects about 97; 2N(1 − 1/N) = 98 is an approximation") was cut from the reveal for learner r8 (two theory numbers and a formula with nothing on the stage for them; reveal over 90 words). No learner sentence uses it now. cm-life-genetics-evolution may restore a shorter form (W-184).

claims.text: Every step back, some lines pick the same mother and join; joined lines never split, so with only 50 women, joins continue until one line is left.
claims.source: Each woman has exactly one mother, so two lines that share an ancestor share every earlier ancestor; with a finite population of 50 the number of lines can only fall, and falls with positive probability each generation while more than one line remains, so it reaches 1 with probability 1. · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Re-derived: one mother per woman, so joined lines share all earlier ancestors; line count is non-increasing and falls with positive probability whenever k > 1, so it reaches 1 almost surely (all 1,000 seeded runs did). | v3 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): learner r8 phone fit: reveal now "Every step back, some lines pick the same mother and join; joined lines never split. With only 50 women, joins continue until one line is left." ('to choose from' cut). Meaning unchanged. Needs re-check.

claims.text: The common mother was not alone: 49 other women lived beside her, but their maternal lines did not reach today.
claims.source: The model keeps 50 women in every generation; at the meeting generation only one of them is a maternal ancestor of all of today's 50 women, and by definition no other woman of that generation has a maternal line to today. · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Re-derived: N = 50 in every generation; at the meeting generation every present-day maternal line passes through the one mother, so none of the other 49 has a maternal line to today. | v3 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): learner r8: the '+ 49 others' row label is now 12 px in a 360-wide viewBox (about 10.7 px on a phone) and, when the reveal opens the slider is set to at least generation 99 (the learner may move it again), so the row the reveal sentence points at is on the stage. Text unchanged. Needs re-check of the stage behaviour.

claims.text: It is the drift from 'Nobody wins, one colour takes over', run backward.
claims.source: Same haploid Wright–Fisher sampling (each generation a random draw of parents from the last), traced backward instead of forward. Source: the published lesson life/same-genes-different-drift, claim life.same-genes-different-drift.c1. · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: life/same-genes-different-drift (published, title 'Nobody wins, one colour takes over') is haploid Wright-Fisher: each new individual copies a parent drawn at random from the last generation; this lesson traces the same draw backward. | WITHDRAWN v2 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave G): sentence removed from the reveal (r7: dangling reference to another lesson for learners who did not take it).

claims.text: Stage rule: 50 women per generation; each has a random mother from the one before.
claims.source: The lesson's model (brief all-lines-meet-in-one-mother, company/courses/ncm/briefs.md, life.genetics-evolution #3); a toy model, not human data. · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Stage rule text matches verbatim; N = 50, mother = floor(rng() x 50) per line.

claims.text: Over the same 1,000 seeds (7001-8000) with the same draw rule, all lines met on average 46 generations back with 25 women and 197 with 100 (96 with 50): double the women, roughly double the wait, about 2N generations. Reveal: "With 25 women, 46; with 100, 197: double the women, roughly double the wait, about 2N generations." Stage: "Mean wait: 25 women: 46 · 50: 96 · 100: 197".
claims.source: meanFor(n) in Demo.tsx (meetTime with n women per generation, seeds 7001-8000), shown on the stage as 'Mean wait: 25 women 46 · 50 women 96 · 100 women 197' after 'Same with 25 and 100 women'. Builder run 2026-10-14 (node strip-types, same function): 25 -> 46.17 (median 39), 50 -> 96.03 (median 84), 100 -> 197.43 (median 171); 2N(1 − 1/N) gives 48, 98, 198. Seeds are the existing run block, not chosen for these sizes. Added v2 (demo-builder, wave G) for the r7 finding that 'about 2N' was told with one N. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node port of meetTime/mulberry32, seeds 7001-8000: 25 women mean 46.175 (46), 50 women 96.033 (96), 100 women 197.433 (197); medians 39, 84, 170-171; standard errors 0.8, 1.6, 3.4; exact expectations 47.2, 97.0, 196.7; 2N = 50, 100, 200. meanFor uses the same RUN_SEEDS block as runThousand (seed choice as stated). The sizes milestone is required, so the reveal's 'With 25 women ... 46, with 100, 197' always prints and matches the Mean wait row. | v3 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): learner r8: reveal sentence and stage strip line reworded for the 90-word budget and one-line strip; values unchanged. Needs re-check.

recall.question: Everyone alive today descends, mother to mother, from one woman who lived long ago. What does that say about her time?
options: She was the only woman alive then
She lived among many other women whose maternal lines later died out
She must have lived only a few generations ago
recall.why: Traced back, maternal lines keep joining whenever two people share a mother, until one line is left. That woman had many contemporaries; their lines simply did not survive to today.
